question: What is the acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the Earth?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**9.8 m/s²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the Earth is **9.8 m/s²**.
 
• This value represents the acceleration that objects experience when falling freely towards the Earth.
 
• The value of 9.8 m/s² is derived from the **gravitational constant (G)** and the **mass and radius of the Earth**.
 
• **Gravity **is a force that attracts two bodies towards each other, and it is crucial for maintaining the orbits of planets and satellites.
 
• The standard value of 9.8 m/s² is used in various calculations in physics and engineering, such as projectile motion and free-fall equations.
 
• The unit of acceleration due to gravity is **meters per second squared (m/s²)**.
